findings.summary: Forcing session DateStyle to 'ISO, MDY' changes how ambiguous date/time literals inside arbitrary user SELECT queries are parsed by Postgres (not just how output is formatted), which can silently change query results compared to the datasource's own configured/default DateStyle.
findings.evidence: await client.query(`SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'`); is executed unconditionally before running the user's arbitrary SELECT query. DateStyle's second component (MDY/DMY/YMD) governs interpretation of ambiguous string-to-date casts (e.g. '01/02/2025'::date) appearing anywhere in the user's SQL, not just the rendering of already-typed date columns. If the target database's configured DateStyle differs (e.g. 'ISO, DMY'), this override silently changes the semantic meaning of such literals in the user's query versus running it directly against their DB.

findings.summary: The custom getTypeParser override ignores the format argument for the raw-text OIDs, always returning a text-mode identity parser regardless of whether binary wire format was requested for that column.
findings.evidence: const datasourceTypeParser: typeof types.getTypeParser = (oid, format) => RAW_TEXT_OIDS.has(oid) ? (value: string) => value : getDefaultParser(oid, format); For DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ the identity (value) => value is returned even when format === 'binary', in which case the runtime value would actually be a Buffer of binary-encoded bytes rather than a string; treating it as already-text would silently corrupt the value instead of decoding it. Currently unreachable given the driver's default text protocol usage, but the guard does not defend against it.

findings.summary: RAW_TEXT_OIDS only covers scalar DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ OIDs; the corresponding array OIDs (_date, _timestamp, _timestamptz) are not included, so a SELECT returning an array of dates would still go through the default parser and remain subject to the timezone-shift bug this change is meant to fix.

executeQuery now issues two extra session-level SET statements (SET TimeZone, SET DateStyle) on every query against a customer-configured Postgres datasource. Existing DataSource records created before this change (any already-connected external database, especially ones fronted by a transaction-pooling PgBouncer/pgpool or by a restricted role that disallows SET) will start failing where they previously worked, since SET requires a session-scoped connection and this code path had no such requirement before.
findings.evidence: await client.query(`SET TimeZone = 'UTC'`); await client.query(`SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'`); — added unconditionally to executeQuery, run against every existing/previously-working DataSource record, not gated by any capability check.

findings.summary: The DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ text format returned to API consumers changed from a JS Date's JSON representation (e.g. 2025-06-15T05:30:00.000Z, always UTC/ISO-8601-with-T) to raw Postgres text under 'ISO, MDY' DateStyle (e.g. 2025-06-15 05:30:00+00, space-separated, no milliseconds, offset without colon). Any downstream consumer of QueryResult.rows that previously relied on ISO-8601-with-'T' formatting (date parsing, string matching, snapshot tests) will silently receive a differently-shaped string. No non-test consumer parses date columns today, but this is a public API response shape change with no callers audited beyond the two files in the diff.
findings.evidence: rows: Record<string, unknown>[] — type unchanged, but the runtime string format of date/timestamp values in this field changed; no frontend/backend consumer of QueryResult.rows was found to assert on the old Date/ISO-with-T shape, but any future or external integration keying off it will break silently.

findings.summary: New exported `toCell` utility (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts) has zero dedicated unit tests in its own package, and one of its two non-trivial branches (the `val instanceof Date` → ISO-string branch) is never exercised by any test in the diff.
findings.evidence: packages/sheets has no *.spec.ts referencing `toCell` or `loadQueryResults` (grep found nothing). The only exercise of `toCell` is indirectly through packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts, which requires a live Postgres and is skipped when DATABASE_URL isn't set. Even there, the Date branch is never hit: datasource.service.ts overrides the pg type parser for exactly the three OIDs (DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ) that would otherwise produce JS `Date` instances (RAW_TEXT_OIDS in datasource.service.ts lines ~19-24), forcing them to raw strings before they ever reach `toCell`. Additionally, since `loadQueryResults` is consumed by the frontend from an HTTP/JSON API response (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/datasource-view.tsx), any Date would already have been serialized to a string by JSON before reaching `toCell` in that path too. So the `instanceof Date` branch added at readonly.ts is effectively untested by any test in this diff, and its behavior (and whether it's even reachable) is unverified.

findings.summary: The new 'check correct cell values for all pg built-in types' test and the pre-existing 'queries real tables with rows' test now overlap almost entirely with a newly-added, near-duplicate test of the same name ('queries real tables with rows' appears twice, back to back, in the same describe block) doing the same table setup/query/cleanup, one asserting via toCell/String and the other via raw toEqual.
findings.evidence: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts: a test named `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` is added at line 114 (verifying via `toCell`), and the pre-existing test with the identical name and near-identical body (verifying via toEqual on {id,name,price}) still exists unmodified at line 309. This looks like a leftover/duplicate rather than an intentional replacement — the old assertion style (`rows` compared with plain JS values) was not updated to reflect the new raw-text type-parser behavior for the fields it touches, and having two identically-named tests doing almost the same thing adds no incremental coverage while creating confusion about which test is authoritative.

findings.summary: Two existing assertions were weakened from full-object equality (`toEqual({ n: 1 })`) to a loose string-coercion check (`String(rows[0].n)).toBe('1')`), reducing the precision of what's verified (e.g. no longer checks there's exactly one key/row shape, or that `n` really is the number 1 vs. some other value that stringifies to '1').
findings.evidence: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts lines 108-111 and ~199-207 change `expect(queryResult.rows).toEqual([{ n: 1 }])` to `expect(String(rows[0].n)).toBe('1')`. Since INT4 is not part of RAW_TEXT_OIDS and is unaffected by the new type-parser change, the original strict assertion would still have passed; the loosened form isn't required by the new behavior and reduces assertion strength.

findings.summary: toCell's generic object fallback leaks Node Buffer's internal JSON shape for BYTEA columns instead of a readable representation
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:32-35 — toCell() JSON.stringify()s any non-Date object, so a BYTEA value (a Node Buffer) renders in a spreadsheet cell as '{"type":"Buffer","data":[222,173,190,239]}' (as asserted by the new e2e test), which is an internal driver representation rather than a spreadsheet-appropriate rendering (e.g. hex) — a display-fit concern for the read-only results grid rather than a logic bug.

verdict.reason: The code at packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:145 unconditionally runs `await client.query(\`SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'\`)` before executing the user's arbitrary SELECT query (wrapped and run at line 148-150), with no guard, per-datasource configuration, or restoration of a prior style. Postgres's DateStyle setting genuinely affects both output formatting AND input parsing of ambiguous date/time string literals (e.g. `'01/02/2025'::date` or implicit casts in WHERE/ORDER BY clauses) for the duration of the session. Since the query the user supplies is run inside this same session after the SET, any ambiguous date literals embedded in that arbitrary SQL will be reinterpreted under MDY convention regardless of the datasource's actual configured DateStyle (which could be DMY), silently altering the semantic result of such literals compared to running the same query directly against the target database. There is no other guard or call path that prevents this from applying to the user query; it's the same client/session used for both the SET and the wrapped SELECT. This is a real, unguarded logic/correctness issue under the Correctness lens (wrong behavior / silently different query results), so I cannot refute it via not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.

verdict.reason: I read the entire docs/design/sheets/datasource.md (lines 1-232) and confirmed the reviewer's evidence: the 'Query Execution' section (lines 156-162) lists only the query-wrap, statement timeout, connection timeout, max rows, and response shape — no mention of the new `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` / `SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'` session statements or the `datasourceTypeParser` override (packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:19-37, 144-145, 204), which are real, present in code and covered by tests (datasource.service.spec.ts:130-131). I grepped the whole doc file for TimeZone/DateStyle/getTypeParser/RAW_TEXT_OIDS and found zero matches, and also checked docs/tasks/** for any companion task doc describing this change — none found. I could not find a counterexample location (another design doc, task doc, or section of datasource.md) that documents this behavior, so I cannot refute the absence claim. However, I also could not conclusively establish it crosses the 'architecture/data-model change' bar in CONTRIBUTING.md (vs. being a scoped bug fix to date/timestamp correctness that wouldn't require a design-doc update) since no linked issue/task doc was available to check how this change was classified, so I'm not fully confident it's a slam-dunk 'major' either. Given I found no counterexample after a genuine wide search but can't be fully certain nothing satisfies the doc-discipline requirement elsewhere in the repo, I record this as unresolved rather than confirmed, per instructions to prefer unresolved over an overreaching confirmation.
